clue.text: Anxious state no good in a street

indicators.note: the words no good are placed inside the words a street, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: A as written plus ST, the usual abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Someone stands nervously out on the road, feeling useless and worried.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a German loanword for a feeling of deep anxiety or dread.

clue.text: Fool is beginning to taunt soldier and aide

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: only the opening letter of taunt is used

parts.note: a soldier ant is the warrior caste of an ant colony, so ant can stand for soldier

explanation.surface: A foolish person starts mocking both a soldier and his helper.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant is a helper, someone who aids another in their work.

clue.text: Sticky stuff almost became solid? Fool!

parts.note: goo is sticky, viscous matter

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for becoming solid is dropped

parts.note: set means hardened or became solid

explanation.surface: Gloopy material nearly hardened, and someone is called an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Goose is an informal term for a silly person, a fool.

clue.text: One who may leak most of speech penned by tense former PM

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: the shortened speech word is enclosed, as in a pen, by the letters for tense and the former PM

parts.note: Clement Attlee was British Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951

indicators.note: the last letter of the speech word is dropped

parts.note: talk is a speech or lecture

explanation.surface: An informant reveals most of an address written by a strained ex-premier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like an adjective for the PM's mood; it is the grammar abbreviation T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattletale is someone who gossips or tells secrets, leaking information about others.

clue.text: Left University to get lowest pay in journalism? That'll make you study

parts.note: a cub reporter is a trainee journalist, so the cub rate is the bottom wage in newspapers

explanation.surface: Quitting a degree course for a junior reporter's wage is presented as a spur to hit the books.
explanation.walkthrough: A cub is a beginner reporter; the cub rate is what such a novice earns.
explanation.definitionFit: To lucubrate is a formal verb for studying laboriously, originally by lamplight late at night.

clue.text: Record brass player being interrupted by new farm animal

indicators.note: the record word is broken into by the letter for new

parts.note: a log is a record, as a ship's log
a horn is a brass instrument, one that plays in the brass section

explanation.surface: A recording of a trumpeter is interrupted by a fresh piece of livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A longhorn is a breed of cattle with long horns, kept on farms and ranches.

clue.text: Shellfish — something you're encouraged to have warmed?

definitions.text: something you're encouraged to have warmed?
definitions.meaning: the phrase warm the ... of your heart means to give deep pleasure

explanation.surface: A seafood item is something you are urged to heat up.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom about warming the heart's chambers uses this word, which also names a seafood mollusc.

clue.text: Profit: billion, and rising as well

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: too means as well

explanation.surface: A financial gain of a billion, and growing besides.
explanation.definitionFit: As an archaic noun and verb, boot means advantage or profit, as in what boots it.

clue.text: Article on curiously violent experimental book

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: curiously signals the letters of violent are arranged in an odd way

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about a strangely violent avant-garde novel.
explanation.definitionFit: An antinovel is fiction that deliberately abandons conventional plot and character, an experimental form.

clue.text: Almost put on power for finish

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for put on is dropped

parts.note: to endue is an old word meaning to put on clothing

explanation.surface: Someone nearly applies energy in order to complete a task.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up is to finish or finally arrive somewhere, the phrasal verb for concluding.

clue.text: Cut and cut around middle of patterns

indicators.note: the shorn letters wrap around the central pair taken from the word patterns

parts.note: shorn means cut, as of a sheep's fleece

indicators.note: the central letters of the eight-letter word patterns are taken

explanation.surface: A dressmaker trims and snips round the centre of some paper patterns.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten something is to make it briefer by trimming it, as with a cut.

clue.text: Obscurity enveloping beginning and end of the hit

indicators.note: the obscurity word wraps around the letters taken from the, holding them inside

parts.note: a cloud is something that obscures, a state of obscurity or gloom

indicators.note: only the first and last letters of the word the are used

explanation.surface: A murky fog surrounds the start and finish of some smash hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouted is the past tense of clout, an informal verb meaning to strike hard.

clue.text: Lately involved with this in an underhand way

indicators.note: letters that are involved are tangled together, so lately and this are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone has recently got mixed up in this, behaving rather sneakily.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something stealthily means doing it furtively and secretly, which is an underhand manner.

clue.text: Political party holding a type of election

indicators.note: the party's initials hold the letter a within them

parts.note: the SNP is the Scottish National Party

explanation.surface: A political party clings to some form of election.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap election is one called suddenly, earlier than expected, giving opponents little warning.

clue.text: Dirty Harry: much of the intention picked up as agitation of the heart

indicators.note: dirty suggests something messed up, so the letters of Harry are scrambled
the last letter of the word the is dropped
in a down clue, picked up means the letters are lifted, reading upwards

parts.note: aim means intention

explanation.surface: The film detective Dirty Harry's intent seems to cause a heart flutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty Harry' looks like Clint Eastwood's cop, but 'Dirty' signals the anagram ARRHY; 'much of' trims THE to TH; 'picked up' turns AIM into MIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrhythmia is a medical condition in which the heartbeat is irregular.

clue.text: European car maker, right-winger, as one hears

parts.note: Audi is a German car manufacturer
a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right

explanation.surface: A list of word associations: a German car brand, a conservative politician, and hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditory describes what relates to the sense of hearing, the way one perceives sounds.

clue.text: What identifies one intending to be late to help others?

definitions.text: What identifies one intending to be late to help others?

parts.words: What identifies one intending to be late to help others?
parts.note: late here means deceased: a card carried by someone who wants their organs used after death

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a badge for someone who plans to arrive behind schedule to assist others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' looks like tardy but means dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a card records a person's wish that their organs be transplanted after they die.

clue.text: Member of RAC or some other club?

definitions.meaning: the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation whose members are motorists
a golf club used for long shots off the tee

explanation.surface: Is this a motoring organisation's member or one belonging to a different society?
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist belongs to a motoring club, and the golfer's longest wood is also called by this name.

clue.text: Register manure and change direction

definitions.note: a verb phrase: to alter the address on a letter

parts.note: a meter reading registers a value, so to read is to register
to dress soil is to apply manure or fertiliser to it

explanation.surface: A gardener records fertiliser use and then switches course.
explanation.definitionFit: To readdress a letter is to change the destination written on it, redirecting it.

clue.text: Traveller in cavalry finally to succeed in fighting

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the fighting word

parts.note: war is fighting

indicators.note: only the last letter of cavalry is used

parts.note: to fare well is to succeed; fare means get on

explanation.surface: A horseman in the cavalry eventually triumphs in combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer is someone who journeys on foot, a traveller.

clue.text: Wee point about Asian city

indicators.note: the point word goes round the city abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: a tine is a prong or point, as of a fork
KL is the common abbreviation for Kuala Lumpur, capital of Malaysia

explanation.surface: A tiny spot on a map surrounds a city in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' looks like 'small', but here it is the informal noun for urinating.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinkle is a childish or informal word for urination, as is wee.

clue.text: Place for heroes: large room surrounded by flowing lava

indicators.note: the large room word sits inside the reshaped lava letters
flowing lava moves and changes shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a hall is a large room, as in a great hall

explanation.surface: A grand chamber sits amid streams of molten rock, a fitting home for heroes.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth Valhalla is Odin's great hall where slain warriors feast forever.

clue.text: Incentive — to visit a mechanic?

definitions.meaning: an inducement, as the vegetable dangled before a donkey
rusting bodywork on a vehicle, ..., is a reason to take it to a garage

explanation.surface: A motivation for taking the car to the garage.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward dangled to encourage effort is called by this vegetable's name, from the donkey and stick image.

clue.text: League Two team, sturdy without intervention of league

indicators.note: the league letter that intervenes in the middle of the sturdy word is removed

parts.note: burly means strongly built and sturdy

explanation.surface: A lower-division football side proves robust without help from the league.
explanation.walkthrough: League Two is the fourth tier of English football; Bury FC played there.
explanation.definitionFit: Bury is a Lancashire town whose football club has played in League Two.

clue.text: Cricketer missing line in greenery?

indicators.note: the cricketer word is missing the line letter

parts.note: a bowler delivers the ball in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricketer without a sightline wonders if he is lost among the foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bower is a shady leafy shelter in a garden, formed of greenery.

clue.text: Incredible soccer teams not initially unhappy about start of football

parts.note: the FA, the Football Association, is the body made up of England's soccer teams

indicators.note: the trimmed unhappy word goes around the opening letter of football
the first letter of the unhappy word is dropped

parts.note: wretched means miserable or unhappy

indicators.note: only the first letter of football is used

explanation.surface: Football clubs, surprisingly, are no longer miserable at kick-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' turns WRETCHED into RETCHED, which goes 'about' F to make RFETCHED.
explanation.definitionFit: A far-fetched story is so improbable that it is hard to believe.

clue.text: Treasure one buried in hospital yard

indicators.note: the word one is placed within the two abbreviations

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone has hidden riches in the grounds of a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treasure' looks like buried loot, but it is a term of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey and treasure are both affectionate names for a loved one.

clue.text: Against leaving barge in Oxford?

indicators.note: the letter for against departs from the barge word

parts.note: to barge is to push, to shove
V is short for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: A protester quits a river barge in the university city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' looks like the city, but is a style of laced shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a type of laced leather shoe, so it is an example of footwear.

clue.text: Withstand article penetrating clothing

indicators.note: the article goes into the middle of the clothing word

parts.note: wear means clothing, as in evening wear
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Something sharp pierces a garment yet the garment holds out.
explanation.definitionFit: To weather a storm or crisis is to survive it, to come through it intact.

clue.text: Affair is an African party in a European city

indicators.note: the party's letters go inside the city's name

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital
the ANC is the African National Congress of South Africa

explanation.surface: A liaison is likened to a South African political gathering held in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a love affair, a romantic relationship between two people.

clue.text: Revolutionary supplier of crossword is one identifying the game

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist revolutionary
a setter is the person who composes a crossword

explanation.surface: A radical compiler of puzzles is said to be the one who identifies the game being played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like a sport or contest, but means birds or animals hunted for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish setter, a gundog, points out where game birds are hiding for hunters.

clue.text: A ship is circling next to ocean depth

indicators.note: the letters for a ship go around the letters for next to

parts.note: A as written plus SS, which stands for steamship
by means beside or next to

explanation.surface: A vessel circles alongside a deep part of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a profound chasm, and in oceanography the abyssal zone is the deep sea floor.
